t.4.25.1: Then the chief ministers of the monkeys gathered around Sugrīva, who was consumed by grief and whose garments were wet, and attended upon him.
t.4.25.2: Having approached the mighty-armed Rāma, whose deeds are done without strain, they all stood with joined palms, like the seers before Pitāmaha.
t.4.25.3: Then Hanumān, son of the Wind, who resembled a golden mountain and whose face shone like the rising sun, spoke these words with joined palms.
t.4.25.4: By your grace, O lord, Sugrīva has obtained this great kingdom of the monkeys, inherited from his father and grandfather and most difficult to attain.
t.4.25.5: Permitted by you, he will enter the auspicious city and, together with his friends, arrange all the affairs.
t.4.25.6: Having bathed according to the prescribed rites with various fragrances and herbs, he will honor you especially with jewels and garlands.
t.4.25.8: Thus addressed by Hanumān, Rāghava, the slayer of enemy heroes, wise and skilled in speech, replied to Hanumān.
t.4.25.7: You should go from here to this delightful mountain cave; gladdening the monkeys, establish your bond with them as their lord.
t.4.25.10: Let the heroic Sugrīva, bull among monkeys, having duly entered the splendid and richly furnished cave, be swiftly consecrated in the kingship.
t.4.25.9: O gentle Hanumān, I shall not enter a village or a city for fourteen years, for I am bound to keep my father's command.
t.4.25.11: Having spoken thus to Hanūmān, Rāma said to Sugrīva: "O hero, consecrate this Aṅgada too in the office of crown prince."
t.4.25.12: This is Śrāvaṇa, the first month of the rains, the month when the waters come; the four months known as the rainy season have now begun, O gentle one.
t.4.25.13: This is not the time for undertaking action; enter the splendid city. I, gentle one, will dwell on this mountain together with Lakṣmaṇa.
t.4.25.14: This mountain cave is delightful and spacious, open to the breezes; it has abundant water, O gentle one, and an abundance of lotuses and water-lilies.
t.4.25.15: When the month of Kārttika has arrived, you must strive for the slaying of Rāvaṇa; this is our agreement, gentle one. Now enter your own dwelling, have yourself consecrated in the kingship, and gladden your friends.
t.4.25.16: Thus permitted by Rāma, Sugrīva, the bull among monkeys, entered the delightful city of Kiṣkindhā, which had been ruled by Vālin.
t.4.25.17: Thousands of monkeys, overjoyed, saluted that lord of the monkeys as he entered, and surrounded him on every side.
t.4.25.18: Then all the subjects, seeing the lord of the monkey hosts, bowed their heads and, with composed minds, fell prostrate upon the earth.
t.4.25.19: The valorous and mighty Sugrīva, having spoken with all the subjects and raised them to their feet, entered the pleasant inner apartments of his brother.
t.4.25.21: For him they brought a pale white parasol adorned with gold, and two white yak-tail whisks with golden handles, bestowing glory.
t.4.25.20: When Sugrīva, the bull among monkeys, had entered and come forth again, his friends consecrated him, just as the immortals consecrated the thousand-eyed Sahasrākṣa.
t.4.25.22: Likewise all kinds of gems, all seeds and medicinal herbs, and the shoots and blossoms of milky-sapped trees.
t.4.25.23: White garments too, and white unguent as well, and fragrant garlands of flowers born on land and born in water.
t.4.25.24: Heavenly sandal pastes and many perfumes of various kinds, unbroken grains of rice and gold, priyaṅgu, honey and ghee.
t.4.25.25: Bringing curd, a tiger skin and a pair of boar-hide sandals, fragrant unguent, and yellow rocanā together with red arsenic, sixteen excellent maidens came there in delight.
t.4.25.27: Then the people versed in sacred mantras, having offered oblations purified by mantras into the kindled fire, Jātavedas, strewn around with kuśa grass,
t.4.25.26: Then, at the proper time and according to the prescribed rites, they, having gratified the foremost of the twice-born with jewels, garments and food, turned to the best of the monkeys.
t.4.25.28: Then, upon the lovely pinnacle of a palace, resting on a golden base, covered with excellent spreads and adorned with colorful garlands,
t.4.25.29: Having seated him, facing east, upon an excellent seat with various mantras, and having gathered waters from rivers and streams and from sacred fords on every side,
t.4.25.30: And the bull-like vānaras, having brought from all the oceans pure and auspicious waters, placed them in golden pitchers.
t.4.25.31: With auspicious bulls' horns and with golden pitchers too, according to the rite laid down in the scriptures and prescribed by the great sages.
t.4.25.33: They consecrated Sugrīva with clear, fragrant water, just as the Vasus consecrated thousand-eyed Vāsava.
t.4.25.32: Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Śarabha, Gandhamādana, Mainda and Dvivida as well, Hanūmān, Jāmbavān and Nala.
t.4.25.34: When Sugrīva had been consecrated, all the great-souled bulls among the monkeys, rejoicing, shouted aloud there in their thousands.
t.4.25.35: Carrying out the word of Rāma, Sugrīva, the bull among monkeys, embraced Aṅgada and had him consecrated as crown prince.
t.4.25.36: And when Aṅgada had been consecrated, the compassionate, great-souled monkeys honored Sugrīva, crying, "Well done, well done!"
t.4.25.37: Crowded with joyful and well-nourished people and adorned with pennants and banners, the delightful city of Kiṣkindhā in the mountain cave became lovely to behold.
t.4.25.38: Then the lord of the monkey army, having reported his great consecration to the great-souled Rāma and having regained his wife Rumā, the valiant one obtained the kingdom, just as the lord of the thirty gods obtained his.
